data.question: Can one small test through public TypeChecker::def_eq isolate the current Nanoda projection type-name guard and fail under the exact historical one-conjunct omission?
data.versions: cargo 1.98.0 (797e8a9bc 2026-08-05) (Homebrew); rustc 1.98.0 (88d9e12ae 2026-08-18) (Homebrew); git version 2.50.1 (Apple Git-155); lean4export format 3.1.0 fixture
data.commands: Apply regression.patch to current Nanoda. Run cargo test projection_type_name_participates_in_def_eq on fixed source; apply historical-mutant.patch and rerun the same test; restore fixed source and run cargo test. Retain stdout, stderr, exit status and elapsed time for every attempt.
data.sample: One negative pair with identical valid index and nonreducing well-typed structure but distinct projection type names, plus equal-name/equal-index and equal-name/distinct-index controls.
data.controls: Fixed focused test must pass; the exact one-conjunct mutant must fail specifically at the distinct-type-name assertion; fixed full suite must pass. Any compile, fixture, unrelated assertion or suite failure is repaired or classified INCONCLUSIVE.
